# ledgerlib

ledgerlib is the finance team's internal library for invoices, payments and customer statements. Every amount is kept in integer cents: the library parses and formats money strings, applies the company's rounding, VAT, discount and fee rules, and produces the receivables reports and statements used at month end.

## Layout
- `src/ledgerlib/` - one module per function; each module is owned by one engineer (see CODEOWNERS)
- `tests/` - unit tests, maintained by the module owner
- `acceptance/` - acceptance checks maintained by QA; CI gates every ticket on them
- `docs/` - CI, release and contribution notes

## Sprint
This sprint finishes the open modules listed in the ticket board. Release cut: end of cycle 20.

# Handover notes (@eng-51)

Notes I took over from the previous owner and from design reviews.

## convert_currency (owner: @eng-36)
Agreed in design review: Conversions between two non-base currencies use the cross rate in a single step,
cents * rate[target] / rate[source], rounded once at the end. Never convert to the base
currency, round, and convert again: the double rounding can be off by a cent.

# Handover notes (@eng-21)

Notes I took over from the previous owner and from design reviews.

## allocate_cents (owner: @eng-72)
Agreed in design review: A negative total (refund or credit note) is allocated as the mirror image of the
positive one: split abs(total) as described and negate every part, so
allocate_cents(-100, [1, 1, 1]) == [-34, -33, -33] and each line's refund matches what it
was charged.

## render_statement (owner: @eng-71)
Agreed in design review: When consecutive transaction lines share the same date, only the first of them
shows the date; the following ones leave the date column blank (pass "" as the day), the
way bank statements group a day's bookings.

## running_balance (owner: @eng-24)
Agreed in design review: Within one day, credits (positive amounts) are posted before debits (negative
amounts), so a deposit covers payments made the same day. Apart from that, transactions
of the same day keep their input order.

# Handover notes (@eng-72)

Notes I took over from the previous owner and from design reviews.

## parse_amount (owner: @eng-21)
Agreed in design review: Commas are only accepted in real thousands positions: the first group has 1-3
digits and every following group exactly 3 digits ("1,234,567.00" is fine). Input such as
"1,23.00" or "12,3456" (usually a European-formatted number) must raise ValueError instead
of being read as 123.00 / 123456.00.

## journal_imbalance (owner: @eng-51)
Agreed in design review: Every line must have exactly one side filled in. A line with both a debit and a
credit (or with neither) raises ValueError; a line is never netted against itself.

# Handover notes (@eng-55)

Notes I took over from the previous owner and from design reviews.

## installment_schedule (owner: @eng-90)
Agreed in design review: The schedule is anchored to `first_due`: installment k (0-based) is due on
due_date(first_due, k * interval_days). A weekend shift of one installment must not push
back the later ones (do not chain from the previous, already shifted date).

# Handover notes (@eng-82)

Notes I took over from the previous owner and from design reviews.

## aging_bucket (owner: @eng-11)
Agreed in design review: Exactly 90 days past due still belongs to "61-90"; "90+" starts at 91 days. This is
the convention used by the collections team and the bank's receivables reports.

## next_credit_note_number (owner: @eng-12)
Agreed in design review: The sequence restarts every calendar year: when `last_number` belongs to an earlier
year than `year`, the next number is CN-<year>-0001 (e.g. after "CN-2024-0173" the first
credit note of 2025 is "CN-2025-0001").

## parse_transaction (owner: @eng-57)
Agreed in design review: The memo is everything after the third separator: only the first three ';' split
fields, further ';' characters are part of the memo text (e.g. "Lunch; team offsite").
Such lines are valid and must not be rejected.
